+  // The Mustache-portability story (the same ADR-022 machinery, narrowed). MinBars

+  // `mustache-spec` engine baseline, flipping under `handlebars` (= mustache.js),

+  mustache: {
+    engine: "minbars",
+    template: "{{#count}}{{count}} unread{{/count}}",
+    data: { count: 0 },
+    finds: 1,
+    expect: [
+      "Engine rule: `mustache-spec`",
+      "1 observed",
+      "the number `0`",
+      "flips under `handlebars`",
+      "mustache.js",
+      "reshape the data",
+      "data path: `count`",
+    ],
+  },
 };

The Mustache story

+

+ The same machinery answers the narrower question Mustache portability turns on. + MinBars renders on the language-agnostic mustache-spec + rule — 0, "", and {} are truthy (as Ruby/Python + Mustache) — but mustache.js follows the handlebars rule instead + (0/"" falsy). So a section over count: 0 shows the + filled branch under MinBars and the empty one under mustache.js: the classic + "it worked in my Mustache, not theirs" bug. +

+ +

+ Analyse reports it against the mustache-spec engine baseline, flipping + under handlebars (which the legend spells out is mustache.js). + The fix is different here: Mustache is logic-less, so there is no inline + (ne …) to write — the analyser steers you to reshape the data (a boolean + flag in the view-model, or normalising 0 to absent), which is exactly what the + JSONata scaffold below generates. +

+
+
